flashcard_questions.q: Which shot frames a character from the chest or shoulders up?
Which shot frames two characters together in one frame?
Which shot films over one character's shoulder to show the other's face?
Which shot shows exactly what a character sees?
Which camera angle is positioned at ground level to create an extreme sense of height?
Which camera angle makes a subject appear weak or inferior?
Which camera angle makes a subject appear heroic and dominant?
Which camera angle makes the horizon appear diagonal?
Which camera movement rises vertically through space for a dramatic reveal?
Which camera movement creates a shaky, raw, documentary-style feel?
Which camera movement uses a stabilised harness so the operator can walk smoothly?
Which camera movement rotates vertically to reveal the height of a building?
Why would a director use a close-up of a character's face?
flashcard_questions.a: To show their emotion and create empathy.

notes: 13 cards: 4 shot-to-framing, 4 angle-to-position-or-effect, 4 movement-to-description, 1 causal. Shot types already carded in the camera-codes lesson were left out so this deck covers the extra vocabulary (bust, two shot, over-the-shoulder, point of view, worm's eye, crane, handheld, steadicam).
